features.name: Token budget pre-flight warning
features.summary: Before LLM send, compute token count vs limit; warn with actionable suggestions (drop/clear). Closes flaw #37 for Phase 22+ and any future cortex chat command.
features.counter_case: Cortex is MCP-first; users don't directly manage a chat context window. Most relevant for Phase 22 web dashboard.

features.name: ChatChunks cache ordering partially closes flaw #40
features.summary: cache_control: ephemeral at section boundaries; stable prefix cached, volatile cur/reminder not. Reduces re-tokenization cost.
features.counter_case: Doesn't eliminate the brevity footer tokens from flaw #40 — only reduces re-tokenization overhead.

features.name: Prompt-cache warming thread
features.summary: Daemon thread sends max_tokens=1 pings every ~30s to prevent Anthropic prompt cache expiry. ~35 lines.
features.counter_case: Adds small API cost per ping; only useful for idle sessions lasting 4+ min. Low priority for batch ingest flows.

features.name: Token estimation via 1% line sampling
features.summary: Sample every (num_lines // 100)th line; extrapolate token count. ~8 lines. <5% error. Avoids full tokenization on large files.
features.counter_case: Cortex skeleton mode already avoids reading large files in full. Optimization pays off mainly on large raw source files.

features.name: Chat history budget: max_input/16 clamped 1k-8k
features.summary: min(max(max_input_tokens / 16, 1024), 8192) — derives history cap from model context window. Larger-context models get more history budget automatically.
features.counter_case: Cortex compress uses fixed thresholds. This heuristic is validated for chat; may not apply directly to knowledge synthesis workflows.

features.name: Windows PowerShell vs CMD parent-process detection
features.summary: Walk psutil process tree to find powershell.exe or cmd.exe; wrap command as 'powershell -Command <cmd>' if PowerShell. Handles nested process hierarchies.
features.counter_case: Adds psutil dependency. Cortex's current shell detection may be adequate for the primary Windows use case.

features.name: ChatChunks ordered message assembly with cache markers
features.summary: Dataclass with 8 named sections assembled in fixed order. cache_control: ephemeral markers added at examples, repo, and chat_files boundaries.
features.counter_case: Requires restructuring Cortex's context assembly pipeline. build_context_pack already has ordering but not this explicit dataclass approach.

features.name: FinishReasonLength assistant prefill continuation
features.summary: When LLM output truncated (finish_reason=length), if model supports assistant_prefill, append partial as assistant message with prefix:True and continue. Enables infinite-length synthesis.
features.counter_case: Cortex's LLM calls are tool-call shaped, not open-ended chat. Applies mainly to long save_synthesis or entity generation flows.

features.name: FileWatcher with AI comment trigger
features.summary: Background watchfiles thread monitors for files with '# ai' or '// ai' comments. On change, auto-adds file to context and interrupts input loop.
features.counter_case: Cortex needs a persistent daemon for this (cortex watch). Requires consistent comment convention across files.

features.name: OAuth onboarding with free/paid tier auto-model selection
features.summary: For new users with no API keys, offer OpenRouter OAuth (PKCE). After auth, check is_free_tier → auto-select free or paid model.
features.counter_case: Cortex is local-first with user's own API keys. OAuth onboarding is Phase 22+ scope (remote dashboard).

features.name: Version check file-mtime TTL sentinel
features.summary: Uses mtime of ~/.aider/caches/versioncheck as a 24h TTL sentinel. No JSON key needed — file existence + mtime is the TTL mechanism.
features.counter_case: Trivially simple; many TTL implementations use a JSON field. The file-mtime approach is a minor implementation detail.

features.name: PageRank on symbol def-ref graph for context relevance
features.summary: Build networkx MultiDiGraph from tree-sitter defs/refs. Run PageRank with personalization (chat files get 50× weight boost). Rank symbols by distributed PageRank score.
features.counter_case: Requires networkx dep and significant implementation (~200 lines). Cortex's entity graph already provides some ranking via import centrality. High effort kills the score despite high severity.

features.name: Third-party analytics SDK tokens embedded in source
features.summary: Mixpanel and PostHog project tokens hardcoded in public source. UUID-prefix sampling (is_uuid_in_percentage) limits collection to ~10% of users.
features.pattern: Third-party telemetry embedded in source + opt-in after launch
features.cortex_implication: Any Phase 22+ telemetry must be 100% opt-in, local-aggregate-only, no third-party SDK tokens in source.

features.name: Should Cortex adopt PageRank-based symbol graph ranking?
features.question: Aider's PageRank approach properly closes flaw #26 but costs effort=3. Is BFS/DFS from entry points (effort=2) good enough, or should we invest in full PageRank?
alternatives: Port aider's networkx PageRank to TypeScript — high effort, closes #26 fully
BFS/DFS from entry-point entities ranked by call count — medium effort, closes #26 partially
Ship planned IDF+BFS (flaw fix #7) as is — low effort, good enough for current scale
